speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you experienced a rear-end collision and now have right groin pain with an abnormal leg position. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and if you are currently in severe pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture.

Based on the mechanism of injury (restrained driver in a rear-end collision), immediate severe groin pain, and the specific finding of an abnormal leg position, a displaced femoral neck fracture is the most likely diagnosis. I will be requesting a hip X-ray and a CT scan to confirm the fracture location and degree of displacement.
